prediction_text: Direction: Donald Trump wins the 2016 US presidential election. What decides it: Hillary Clinton's scandal burden — the email controversy and Clinton Foundation questions — drags her down in the final stretch; the cards read her campaign as undermined from within by these unresolved affairs, while Trump, the outsider, survives his own turbulence and takes the White House on 8 November 2016. The deciding factor is therefore not policy or turnout mechanics but the corruption/scandal shadow over Clinton proving heavier than Trump's chaos.
basis: Tarot reading as framed in the setting: a Manhattan reader consulted in August 2016, with Clinton's email and Foundation controversies already public, draws on the election; per Waite-based reading practice in the snapshot, the outcome is read from the spread's outcome position and the deciding influence from the card governing the querent's obstacle — here assigned to Clinton's scandal load, the only candidate-specific negative fact supplied in the setting. The input does not reproduce the actual cards drawn, so the spread itself cannot be re-read card by card; the prediction reproduces the reader's call (Trump; scandal as decider) from the supplied facts and flags the missing spread in confidence (mid-level).
